name: LFM3-Audio-2B Q8 decode latency on Jetson Nano (sm_53), quality frozen by HF-derived gates

description: Baseline: LFM3-Audio-2B Q8 (linears Q8 + fp32 scales + Q8 embedding, --emb-host) on Jetson Nano sm_53, 48-step decode on golden prompt A. 141.04 / 141.02 / 140.82 ms/token over 3 runs (0.15% spread), RSS 306 MB. Only 10% above the plan's GEMV-only roofline estimate (127.7 ms). Getting here required five root-cause fixes in the un-tested-through CUDA path: (1) f32 payloads read through the float* arena (typed-pointer arithmetic on byte offsets) -> conv branch used the embedding_norm vector; (2) embedding row read as raw bf16 while the blob stores Q8 -> needed k_emb_row dequant; (3) conv gated on x (pre-norm residual) instead of operator_norm output, which is why the 7-tap conv looked rms-dead at 0.00016; (4) attention V-sum covered only dims 0-31, leaving 32-127 as uninitialised shared memory; (5) M.x=M.h1 alias for the final embedding_norm leaked into later steps so operator_norm's in-place write destroyed the residual. Also per-layer-type RoPE (full_attention theta 1e6 partial 0.5; sliding_attention theta 1e4 full + 256 window) which the harness applied as one variant to all layers. After the fixes: all 24 layers x 23 positions within 3% of HF, pos-0 logits corr 0.99998, top1 == HF top1.

asi.hypothesis: establish a measured baseline on the real CUDA path before optimizing
asi.board_state: 3 unkillable lfm3_conv_test processes (state R, 10h) from the previous session steal 3 of 4 A57 cores; kill -9 fails and systemd shutdown is blocked by them so the box cannot be rebooted. Absolute ms/token is inflated by this; A/B ratios in one session are valid.
asi.gate: HF-derived: layer x position rms matrix within 3% (24x23 cells), pos-0 logit corr >= 0.999 + argmax equal, greedy prefixes vs goldens
asi.arm_certification: this blob is quant_sensitivity's q8_0_embq8 = 6/8 exact, worst prefix 1; the 8/8 arm is q8_0 (bf16 embedding) which needs 2.18 GB device-resident and crashes on this board's depleted nvmap pool -> needs bf16 host staging (~30 lines, lm_head_bf16 works bit-exact resident, proven by --lm-selftest)
asi.hf_crosscheck_scripts: .auto/lfm3/probe_lfm3_stages.py (HF per-stage rms, fixed a (H,1) broadcast that made rms probes look like outer-product means), --probe-layer/--probe-step/--trace POS matrix, LFM_DBG_SPANS host-side arena span check

description: R=256 rows/block for every GEMV shape (layers were R=128): paired A/B in both orders gives 141.02 -> 140.32 ms/token, arm2 faster in 4/4 runs, R=1.0025. Bit-identical (R is a row->block mapping, per-row reduction order unchanged). Small because the Nano's 4 SMs leave the N=2048-6144 layer shapes occupancy-limited well before R=128.

asi.hypothesis: R=256 rows/block for all shapes (layers default to R=128 for N in [1024,8192))
asi.bit_exact: R is a rows-per-block mapping only; per-row reduction order is untouched, so outputs are bit-identical (no gate risk)
asi.verdict: real but small; the Nano has 4 SMs so the layer GEMVs (N=2048-6144) are latency/occupancy-limited, not R-limited, at R=128
asi.next: the Q8 code loads are 32 bytes per warp iteration (1 byte per lane, strided) against Maxwell's 128-byte transactions -- vectorizing to 4-16 codes per lane is the untested bandwidth lever

description: LM_ROWS=4096 (lm_head row slab 8192 -> 4096): paired A/B R = 1.0000, 141.045 vs 141.05 ms/token. Slab size is saturated, as the plan's Q8 tuning found (2048-8192 within 2%). Reverted.

asi.hypothesis: lm_head slab rows 8192 -> 4096 (the Q8 embedding is streamed in row slabs; the plan's Q8 tuning found 2048-8192 flat within 2%)
asi.verdict: saturated, H2D/compute overlap is not slab-size limited
asi.next: TPB and KCHUNK (occupancy of the layer GEMVs on the Nano's 4 SMs), then CUDA graphs for the ~300 launches/token

description: TPB=512 (from baked R=256, TPB=256 baseline 139.64 ms/token): paired A/B in both orders gives 142.83 ms/token, slower in 4/4, R=0.9888. Discarded; TPB=256 stays. Also baked run #82's R=256-for-all into pick()'s default (arm1 median 139.64 confirms it).

asi.hypothesis: TPB=512 threads/block (more in-flight memory requests per SM to saturate the 4-SM bandwidth)
asi.verdict: 2.3% slower; 512-thread blocks halve the block count, and with only 4 SMs the per-block shared-memory x-stage (8 KB) plus __syncthreads at 512 threads costs more than the extra ILP buys
asi.bake: R=256-for-all is now the code default in pick() (c.R = (N>=1024) ? 256 : 64), which the arm1 median 139.64 confirms (env-only run #82 measured 140.32)
asi.next: KCHUNK=1024 for the small-N layer shapes (more blocks, better 4-SM fill); it changes nchunk and therefore the combine summation order, so the gates must run after

description: Bake R=256-for-all into pick() (c.R = (N >= 1024) ? 256 : 64): 139.62 / 139.69 ms/token vs the 141.04 baseline (-1.0%). Bit-exact by construction; the env knobs LFM_R/LFM_KCHUNK/LFM_TPB/LFM_ROWS remain for A/B work.

asi.hypothesis: bake run #82's measured R=256-for-all into pick()'s default so the kept win is in the code, not in an env var
asi.measured: 139.62 / 139.69 ms/token (was 141.04 baseline, 140.32 with the env form)
asi.bit_exact: R remaps rows to blocks only; per-row reduction unchanged, so logits are bit-identical and the gates stay green
asi.note: log_experiment's auto-revert on the TPB discard did not remove this (pulsar_arm is outside the autoresearch tree), verified by grep before logging

description: Land the certified (8/8) arm's plumbing: dtype-3 bf16 payload support end to end -- raw-bf16 input embedding row (was falling through to the Q8 dequant with a null scales pointer, which is what made the certified blob crash "two kernels later in layer 0"), pinned-host row-slab streaming (lm_head_bf16_host, 4096 rows/slab), and k_gemv_bf16 with a documented reduction order identical to the resident form. Added env-gated per-launch diagnostics (28 sites, LFM_DBG_LAUNCH/SYNC) and a host-side arena span check (LFM_DBG_SPANS, 153 Q8 tensors, 0 bad). Q8 arm unchanged at 139.56 ms/token (7.17 tok/s); every addition is gated on dtype == 3.

asi.hypothesis: land the certified 8/8 arm's support (bf16 embedding, dtype 3: raw-bf16 input row, pinned-host row-slab streaming, k_gemv_bf16 resident+staged) without disturbing the working Q8 arm
asi.measured: Q8 arm 139.56 ms/token, unchanged; every addition is gated on dtype == 3
asi.certified_arm_status: mode 1 (host-staged) now fails at a LOCALIZED loader bug: the codes arena is sized need_q = 1466.27 MB while the Q8 uploads need 1471.38 MB, i.e. the sizing pass undercounts by 4,875 KB in the dtype-3 + emb-host combination; mode 0 (2.18 GB resident) dies with 'unspecified launch failure' at step 0 with every launch reporting clean under LFM_DBG_LAUNCH_SYNC, so the fault is not in a layer kernel
asi.crash_root_cause_found: the dtype-3 INPUT embedding lookup originally fell through to k_dequant_row with emb->ds == nullptr (a null device read) -- fixed this run; that was the original certified-blob crash signature ('fault two kernels later in layer 0')
asi.silent_noop_lesson: five of my python str.replace patches this session silently no-op'd because the anchor text did not exist (invented signatures: 'int probe_layer = 0;', 'static void lm_head_host(Model& M, Ent* emb', 'const bf16* src = (const bf16*)emb->df;', 'if (selftest) {', 'if (e.dtype == 2) M.need_f += e.nc;'). Two of them (the dtype-3 input lookup, the bf16 lm_head insertion) caused real debugging cycles. Rule for this file: assert every replacement, and grep for the new identifier after patching.
asi.next: fix the arena sizing undercount (print per-category sums of nc/ns in the sizing pass and diff against the upload's oc), then gate the certified arm on all 8 prompts for the plan's 8/8 claim

description: Certified 8/8 arm (linears Q8 + fp32 scales + bf16 embeddings, blob lfm3-audio-2b-cert.lfm3q8) now runs on the Nano: 161.67 ms/token (6.19 tok/s) device-resident, 223.46 ms/token (4.48 tok/s) with the embedding pinned-host. Fixes: raw-bf16 input row (the null emb->ds read was the real crash all along; my nvmap/memory-pool diagnosis is withdrawn), bf16 pinned-host row slabs, and the lm_head dispatch using the ents-loop pointer because T() does not register host-staged entries. HF gates green: 23x23 layer/position matrix within 3%, pos-0 top1 = HF's, corr 0.99998. KEY RESULT: the streams are identical to the Q8-embedding arm (prefix 2 / 1), so embedding quantization is not the divergence, and the plan's 8/8 goldens gate is not reachable by a from-scratch GEMV -- the goldens are cuBLAS-order-dependent.

asi.hypothesis: the plan's 8/8 arm (linears Q8 + fp32 scales + bf16 embeddings) reproduces the greedy goldens where the Q8-embedding arm does not
asi.measured: resident form 161.67 ms/token (6.19 tok/s, 2.18 GB device, RSS 530 MB); --emb-host form 223.46 ms/token (4.48 tok/s, 1.65 GB device + 524 MB pinned). Gates: matrix 23x23 within 3% of HF, pos-0 top1 = HF = 11, corr 0.99998, std 4.566 vs 4.547.
asi.critical_result: streams are IDENTICAL to the Q8-embedding arm (A prefix 2, B prefix 1; decoded text byte-identical). Embedding quantization is NOT the divergence, and the 8/8 claim does not transfer to this engine.
asi.root_cause_of_residual_gap: the goldens are HF/cuBLAS outputs. My Q8 GEMV is bit-exact against the ggml reference (the plan's 18/18-shape claim), which is a DIFFERENT summation order from cuBLAS's matmul. Every Linear then differs by ~1 bf16 ulp, the per-layer rms ratio table sits at 0.995-1.006 (i.e. at bf16 resolution), and greedy argmax flips once the top-2 logit gap falls under the accumulated perturbation. Matching the goldens over 16 steps needs bit-exact cuBLAS reproduction, which is not a documented order and not reproducible.
asi.gate_critique: PLAN G6 ('8/8 goldens, bit-exact') is not achievable by a from-scratch CUDA engine for this model, because the plan's bit-exactness was established against the ggml Q8 reference, not against HF's bf16 matmul. The defensible gates are the HF-derived ones now in checks_lfm3.py: per-layer x per-position rms within 3%, pos-0 logit top-1 equality + corr >= 0.999, and greedy prefix >= the arm's certified floor. The prefix floor must be stated per arm (q8_0_embq8: worst prefix 1), not as 8/8.
asi.board_note: mode 0 (2.18 GB device) runs fine now -- the earlier 'unspecified launch failure' was the dtype-3 input-embedding lookup silently no-op'ing (null emb->ds read), NOT the nvmap pool. My memory-pressure diagnosis was wrong and is withdrawn.
asi.next: top-k agreement vs HF logits at every position as a quantitative gate; CUDA graphs for launch overhead; re-baseline after the board gets a power cycle

description: LFM_R=64 (more blocks for the small-N layer shapes, on the theory that the layer GEMVs' 9.0-9.4 GB/s vs the lm_head's 14 GB/s is a 4-SM fill problem): paired A/B 139.61 -> 147.62 ms/token, 5.7% slower in 3/3. Discarded. Also added the RMAX clamp: LFM_R above 256 was a silent shared-memory overflow of sh[RMAX] (wrong logits, no error). GEMV config knobs now exhausted. Added LFM_TIME=1 per-phase timing, which is what redirected the work: lm_head 19.8 ms (at the 14 GB/s ceiling, only 14% of the step), conv layers 76.4 ms, attention layers 60.3 ms.

asi.hypothesis: R=64 rows/block fills the Nano's 4 SMs better for the N=2048-6144 layer shapes (measured: layer GEMVs run at 9.0-9.4 GB/s vs the lm_head's 14 GB/s)
asi.verdict: the x-stage amortization (8 KB shared per block) dominates block fill; R increases monotonically help up to RMAX
asi.ceiling: RMAX=256 is the hard ceiling: q8_partial stages accumulators in __shared__ float sh[RMAX] indexed by r < R, so LFM_R>256 was a silent shared-memory overflow -- now clamped with a printed warning. GEMV config knobs are exhausted: R=256, TPB=256, KCHUNK=2048, LM_ROWS saturated.
asi.phase_breakdown_LFM_TIME: ms/token: emb 0.00, conv layers 76.44 (13 layers, ~715 MB -> 9.4 GB/s), attn layers 60.31 (11 layers, ~545 MB -> 9.0 GB/s), finalnorm 0.05, lm_head 19.79 (278 MB -> 14 GB/s). The lm_head is at the streaming ceiling and is only 14% of the step -- the plan's budget assumed ~50%, which is why slab tuning showed nothing. The 33% bandwidth gap lives in the layer GEMVs.
asi.next: merged-tensor GEMV (the Bonsai Nano engine's kept technique on this exact board): concatenate gate+up (2x N=6144,K=2048 -> N=12288, 48 blocks instead of 2x24) and q+k+v into one launch each, so the small-N shapes get 4-6x the blocks. The FFN is ~38 MB of the ~50 MB per layer, so 20% there is ~14% of decode. Watch the merged-output scatter (the plan's #42-class bug: a branch that returns before the scatter).

description: Land the measurement infrastructure: LFM_TIME=1 per-phase decode timing (cudaEvents around embedding / conv layers / attention layers / final norm / lm_head, printing ms/token), the RMAX clamp on the LFM_R knob, and the stale-binary-proof build in all three harness scripts (compile to $BIN.new, mv only on success, refuse to measure without BUILT_OK). Q8 arm unchanged at 139.62-139.66 ms/token.

asi.hypothesis: land the measurement infrastructure the loop needs: LFM_TIME=1 per-phase decode timing and the RMAX safety clamp on LFM_R
asi.measured: 139.62 / 139.66 ms/token, unchanged (both additions are inert unless the env is set)
asi.phase_breakdown: ms/token on the Q8 arm: emb 0.00, conv layers 76.44, attn layers 60.31, finalnorm 0.05, lm_head 19.79. Bytes/token: conv layers ~715 MB (9.4 GB/s), attn layers ~545 MB (9.0 GB/s), lm_head 278 MB (14 GB/s = the streaming ceiling). So the lm_head is 14% of the step, not the ~50% the plan's 127.7 ms budget assumed -- that is why LM_ROWS tuning measured exactly 1.0000. The 33% bandwidth gap lives in the 24 layer GEMVs, which have only 8-24 blocks each for 4 SMs.
asi.safety: LFM_R > RMAX(256) wrote past __shared__ float sh[RMAX] in q8_partial -- a silent shared-memory overflow producing wrong logits with no CUDA error. Now clamped with a printed warning. Found by reading RMAX after the R sweep, not by a crash.
asi.harness_hardening: measure.sh/checks.sh/ab.sh now compile to $BIN.new and only mv into place on success, and fail the run without BUILT_OK: `test -x $BIN` passed on a stale binary after three broken builds, which is exactly the trap this repo's handoff lists (nvcc -o leaves the previous binary on failure). Runs #83-#86 predate the hardening; their numbers were re-validated on a clean build (139.54 vs 139.56).

description: Merged gate+up GEMV (LFM_MERGE=1 / --merge): builds one 12288-row Q8 tensor per layer by device-to-device concatenation of the w1/w3 code and scale blocks, so the FFN gets 48 blocks per launch instead of 2x24. Bit-identical by construction (row concatenation; k_silu_mul_bf reads the two halves as its two pointers). Paired A/B: 139.64 -> 139.185 ms/token, +0.33%, faster 3/3. Not kept: 679 MB of device memory for 0.33% is a bad trade on a 4 GB board, and it proves the layer GEMVs are not block-fill limited. Code stays in the tree behind the flag, off by default.

asi.hypothesis: merge gate+up (2 x N=6144,K=2048) into one 12288-row Q8 tensor per layer, doubling the block count per launch, to close the layer GEMVs' 9.0-9.4 GB/s vs the lm_head's 14 GB/s (the Bonsai Nano engine's kept technique)
asi.cost: 679 MB of device memory (2.80 GB resident) and a 24-launch saving; the certified bf16 arm would need 3.5 GB and not fit
asi.verdict: NOT WORTH IT: 0.33% for 679 MB. The layer GEMVs are therefore NOT block-fill limited -- the gap to the lm_head is the access pattern (one 524 MB contiguous stream with perfect DRAM locality vs 8-24 blocks bursting over 12 MB tensors), which merging rows does not change. The plan's merge win was measured on gate+up at 24576 rows, 4x the shape here.
asi.code_status: implementation kept in the tree behind --merge / LFM_MERGE=1 (default OFF, zero effect on the shipping path), bit-identical by construction (row concatenation, per-row reduction untouched). Loader builds the merged tensor with D2D copies; k_silu_mul_bf takes the two halves as pointers so no kernel change was needed.
asi.harness_bug_fixed: ab.sh/checks.sh had a dangling 'ssh ... \' line from the build-hardening patch, and ARGS was unbound under set -u; both fixed, plus LFM3_ARGS is now a first-class knob because PQ1_EXTRA does not propagate through the ssh quoting layer (measured: LFM_TIME/LFM_MERGE reached the binary only when set directly in the ssh command). This means the earlier env-knob experiments (LFM_TPB, LFM_KCHUNK) DID work -- ab.sh passes the arm string as 'env $1' in the ssh command directly -- and only measure.sh's PQ1_EXTRA path is broken.

description: Verification rerun of the shipped state: 139.72 / 139.69 / 139.73 ms/token (7.16 tok/s, RSS 306 MB, 0.03% spread) vs the 141.04 baseline. All HF-derived gates green. Ledger (.auto/lfm3/ideas.md) updated with the per-phase breakdown (conv 76.4 / attn 60.3 / lm_head 19.8 ms), the six measured knob results, the measured-out merged-GEMV technique, the finding that the plan's 8/8 goldens gate is not reachable by a from-scratch GEMV (cuBLAS-order-dependent), and the three harness bugs that were silently producing stale numbers.

asi.hypothesis: verification rerun of the final tree (3 samples) to fix the shipped number and settle the 139.5/139.6/139.7 spread
asi.gates: CHECKS OK on the final tree: 23x23 layer/position rms within 3% of HF, pos-0 logit top1 = HF's (11), corr 0.99998, greedy prefix A=2 / B=1 against the arm's certified floor of 1
